beginner.summary: For learners who can write loops, functions and conditionals in Python or Java and want a language-neutral foundation in data structures, algorithms and interview problem solving. Covers Big-O reasoning, arrays and strings, two pointers and sliding window, prefix sums, searching and sorting, hash maps, linked lists, stacks and queues, recursion, binary trees and binary search trees, a repeatable interview method, and a capstone that packages a tested mini algorithm library with a mock interview.
prerequisites: Writes small programs with loops, functions, lists or arrays and conditionals in Python 3 or Java 17 or later
Runs commands in a terminal, for example python3 file.py, javac and java, or git status
Has a laptop with Python 3.12 or later or a JDK 21 or later, plus an editor such as Visual Studio Code or IntelliJ IDEA
outcomes: Estimate time and space complexity of loops, recursion and library calls, and confirm the estimate with timing experiments
Implement arrays, hash maps, linked lists, stacks, queues, sorting and binary search from scratch and test them with pytest or JUnit 5
Solve entry-level interview problems on strings, arrays, lists and trees using two pointers, sliding window, hashing and recursion
Explain a solution out loud in the order clarify, example, brute force, optimize, code, test and state its complexity

subtopics: What an algorithm is and how correctness differs from efficiency

Common classes: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n^2), O(2^n)

days.lab_task: Write two Python functions that detect a duplicate in a list: one with nested loops and one with a set. Time both with python3 -m timeit for n = 1000, 2000 and 4000 distinct values, tabulate the results, and compute the ratio between each size and the next to show roughly 4x growth for the nested version and 2x for the set version.
days.deliverable: Complexity worksheet with the timing table, growth ratios and a one-line Big-O justification for each function
checks: Nested-loop duplicate check run with n doubled from 2000 to 4000
Run time grows by roughly 3.5x to 4.5x
Set-based duplicate check run with n doubled from 2000 to 4000
Run time grows by roughly 1.5x to 2.5x
A loop with i doubling from 1 until i >= n for n = 1,048,576
The loop body runs exactly 21 times, so the loop is O(log n)
Counter value printed by the script
objectives: Classify a function as O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n) or O(n^2) by counting operations
Distinguish time complexity from space complexity
Validate a Big-O estimate with a timing experiment

intermediate.summary: For learners who have finished core data structures and can solve easy problems, and now need the pattern toolkit behind medium interview questions. Covers binary search on answers, monotonic stacks and queues, heaps and top-K problems, tries, intervals and sweep line, greedy proofs, backtracking, bit manipulation, graph traversal, topological sort, union-find, Dijkstra, dynamic programming from memoization to tabulation, tree recursion, and timed mock rounds that end in a pattern playbook capstone.
prerequisites: Implements arrays, hash maps, linked lists, stacks, queues, binary trees and basic sorts in Python 3 or Java 21 and states their Big-O costs
Solves easy interview problems with two pointers, sliding window or hashing and writes pytest or JUnit 5 tests
Reads recursive code and draws a call tree for a small input
outcomes: Choose among binary search, heaps, monotonic stacks, greedy, backtracking, graph search and dynamic programming from a problem statement and its constraints
Implement BFS, DFS, topological sort, union-find and Dijkstra with correct complexity and verify them against brute-force checkers
Convert a recursive solution to memoization and then to bottom-up tabulation, and reduce its space where possible
Solve medium problems in 25 to 30 minutes under mock interview conditions while explaining trade-offs

advanced.summary: For engineers who solve most medium problems and want depth for hard interviews, competitive programming and performance-critical code. Covers amortised analysis, AVL, red-black and B-trees, segment and Fenwick trees, sparse tables, Bellman-Ford and Floyd-Warshall, minimum spanning trees, strongly connected components and bridges, network flow and matching, A* search, KMP, Z, rolling hash, suffix arrays and Aho-Corasick, bitmask and tree DP, randomised and probabilistic structures, geometry, NP-hardness and approximation, external-memory and streaming algorithms, and custom data structure design, ending in an algorithm engineering portfolio.
prerequisites: Solves medium problems on graphs, heaps, intervals and dynamic programming in Python 3 or Java 21 within 30 minutes
Implements BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, union-find and tabulated DP from memory and verifies them with randomised tests against brute force
Reads a recurrence and states the time complexity of recursive algorithms, including the divide and conquer case
outcomes: Prove amortised and worst-case bounds and match them with measurements, such as AVL height, flip counts and Bloom filter false-positive rates
Implement range-query structures, flow algorithms, string matching automata and advanced graph algorithms with randomised verification against brute force
Reason about hardness, choose approximation, heuristic or exact bitmask methods, and measure the approximation ratio
Design interview-grade custom data structures such as LRU and LFU caches with O(1) operations and perform staff-level mock interviews
